title: D1: Confirm repo identity and org
body:
**RESOLVED 2026-08-02:** retain `TheDancingDeveloper-org/NGMS` as the canonical source repository and retain the existing `ghcr.io/thedancingdeveloper-org/ngms` image path.

The former source organization is not the canonical route. This avoids breaking source links and image consumers while the compatibility work is pre-alpha.

**Acceptance:** decision recorded in this issue; §10.3/§10.4 of `docs/UNIFIED-ARR-PLAN.md` updated.

title: D2: MariaDB 11.x or MySQL 8 as the pinned target [RESOLVED: MariaDB 11.4 LTS]
body:
**RESOLVED 2026-08-02: MariaDB, pinned to 11.4 LTS.**

T24 may use MariaDB's `RETURNING` support opportunistically to reduce the 78-site rewrite, but **new code must be written `RETURNING`-free** so a later SQLite or MySQL 8 backend stays cheap.

**Remaining acceptance:** version pinned in `docs/DATABASE.md`, `CONFIGURATION.md` and the CI service container.

title: D3: Relicense MIT to GPL-3.0 [RESOLVED: GPL-3.0]
body:
**RESOLVED 2026-08-02: GPL-3.0.**

Accepted with the consequence understood — this forecloses a closed-source commercial edition.

**Remaining acceptance:** T3 (LICENSE file + `Cargo.toml` `license` field) and T27 (source headers) executed.

title: D4: Ratify the product scope freeze list [RESOLVED: scope freeze ratified]
body:
**RESOLVED 2026-08-02: freeze list ratified as written in §4.3 of the plan.**

Frozen: `stackarr-stream`, Stremio routes, `stackarr-bootstrap`. Deferred: discover/trending/requests/watchlist. Core: engines, Cardigann, migrate.

'Freeze' = keeps compiling and stays tested, accepts no new features, revisited after P5. A PR adding functionality to a frozen subsystem should be rejected on those grounds alone.

**Remaining acceptance:** enforced at PR review.

title: D5: How is MariaDB delivered to end users
body:
Sonarr/Radarr need no external database. Requiring one is an adoption tax on the NAS audience our memory-footprint story targets.

Options: bundle MariaDB in-container via s6-overlay (recommended), external only, or both.

**Acceptance:** decision recorded; reflected in `docker/` and Appendix A's one-command install criterion.

title: D6: Update policy for `=`-pinned crates.io dependencies
body:
**RESOLVED 2026-08-02:** keep `nzb-*`, `nzbdav-*`, and `swarmforge*` dependencies exact-pinned. Dependabot and Renovate group them into weekly reviewed update pull requests.

This preserves reproducibility without recreating silent upstream drift.

**Acceptance:** automation config explicitly matches the published engine packages.

title: D7: Align project naming
body:
**RESOLVED 2026-08-02:** StackArr is the product and crate-family name. The public repository remains `NGMS`, the existing GHCR package remains `ngms`, and the torrent engine remains `swarmforge`.

The deliberate divergence is documented in README and repository guidance, preserving established links and consumers.

title: D8: Does Indexarr merge in or stay separate
body:
`stackarr-indexer` integrates Indexarr today. It overlaps heavily with the Prowlarr-replacement story.

**Acceptance:** decision recorded; affects P3 indexer work and the Prowlarr façade scope.

title: D9: Multi-instance semantics and reported version string
body:
Arr users commonly run two instances (1080p / 4K). Does one StackArr present as two Sonarrs, or does the unified model make that obsolete?

Also: clients gate features on `/api/v3/system/status` version. Pick it deliberately.

**Acceptance:** instance-identity design and version string recorded before T39-T41.

title: T1: Configure repo metadata and retire the stale checkout
body:
Set an honest pre-alpha repository description and add `sonarr`, `radarr`, `prowlarr`, `bittorrent`, `trash-guides`, and `media-automation` topics.

The disjoint legacy shared checkout must remain untouched under the workspace migration policy. Contributors and agents use a clean checkout of canonical GitHub `main` instead.

**Acceptance:** description + topics set; canonical checkout guidance recorded.

title: T2: README: honest status, compatibility promise, public DoD
body: **Acceptance:** README states pre-alpha/not-yet-usable plainly, describes the arr compatibility goal, and embeds Appendix A as a public checklist.

title: T3: Add LICENSE (GPL-3.0)
body:
D3 resolved: **GPL-3.0**.

**Acceptance:** `LICENSE` present; `Cargo.toml` `license` field matches; GitHub detects it.

title: T4: CONTRIBUTING.md encoding the TDD standard
body:
§6.2 as binding policy: red-first from spec, golden files as contract, mandatory `fmt`/`clippy -D warnings`/`test` gates, no `#[allow]` without a named reason.

**Acceptance:** file present and referenced from the PR template.

title: T5: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and SECURITY.md
body:
This software stores indexer and download-client credentials, so a disclosure path is not optional.

**Acceptance:** both files present; SECURITY.md names a contact and expected response time.

title: T6: Correct CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md drift
body:
Three false claims on `main` (§2.5): `torrent/` described as vendored (it is a dead directory, engine comes from crates.io `swarmforge`); `usenet/` described as vendored (the directory no longer exists); 'PostgreSQL 17 (required), never use SQLite' (superseded by the MariaDB decision).

**Acceptance:** file matches `Cargo.toml` reality; T29 can then enforce it.

title: T7: docs/API-COMPATIBILITY.md
body: **Acceptance:** documents target API versions (Sonarr v3, Radarr v3, Prowlarr v1), what is and is not implemented, and a per-client support matrix (Overseerr, Bazarr, Recyclarr, nzb360, Homepage).

title: T8: docs/TESTING.md
body: **Acceptance:** documents the test tiers (unit, property, conformance, e2e), how to run each, and how to add a conformance golden file.

title: T9: Branch protection, required checks, CODEOWNERS
body: **Acceptance:** `main` blocks direct push; PR + green CI required; linear history; required checks include lint/test/build (and conformance once T30-T34 land); CODEOWNERS present.

title: T10: Issue and PR templates
body:
Templates: `bug`, `feature`, `compat-gap`, `provider`, `decision`. PR template checklist: tests added, gates pass, docs updated, no new vendored code.

**Acceptance:** templates render correctly when opening a new issue/PR.

title: T11: Ensure dependency automation watches the pinned engine crates
body:
`nzb-*`, `nzbdav-*`, and `swarmforge*` remain exact-pinned and are matched explicitly by grouped weekly Dependabot/Renovate update rules. This is the control that prevents the silent drift described in §2.4.

**Acceptance:** automation is scheduled and its package patterns cover every published engine pin.

title: T12: Extend the dependency-boundary CI check to forbid re-vendoring
body:
`ci.yml` already has a 'Verify public dependency boundary' step. Extend it: **fail if any `crates/` subdirectory duplicates a crate available as a published dependency.**

**Acceptance:** check fails on a deliberately re-vendored crate; passes on `main` after T15.

title: T13: Create the Projects v2 board
body:
Labels (31) and milestones (P0-P7, numbers 1-8) already exist — do not recreate.

**Acceptance:** board created with custom fields Phase, Area, Size (XS-XL), Risk, Spec-source; all issues added.

title: T14: Verify a clean clone builds on a stock runner
body:
CI is green on self-hosted `node-b`, but an outside contributor cannot get CI on a fork. Confirm `cargo build --workspace` succeeds from a clean clone on `ubuntu-latest`.

**Acceptance:** documented result; any homelab-only dependency identified.

title: T15: Delete crates/torrent/
body:
44,197 LOC and 396 tests that are **not a workspace member** and never compile or run. The torrent engine comes from crates.io as `swarmforge`.

**Acceptance:** directory gone; `cargo build --workspace` and full test suite unchanged; T12's check passes.

title: T16: Audit the `=`-pinned crates.io dependencies
body:
Seven `nzb-*` crates plus `swarmforge` are exact-pinned. Confirm each pin is the intended version and record why exact pinning is used.

**Acceptance:** audit recorded; pins either confirmed or bumped with tests green.

title: T17: Add rust-toolchain.toml
body: **Acceptance:** local and CI resolve the same toolchain; version recorded in CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: T18: Add a justfile
body:
Mirror rdpapp: `check`, `test`, `test-compat`, `test-e2e`, `conformance`, `smoke`.

**Acceptance:** every gate in CONTRIBUTING.md is runnable as a single `just` target.

title: T19: Extend ci.yml
body:
Add: conformance job, coverage ratchet, MariaDB service container, multi-arch build (linux/amd64, linux/arm64, musl). Move `lint` and `test` to `ubuntu-latest` so forks get CI; keep `container`/deploy self-hosted.

**Acceptance:** all jobs green; a fork PR gets CI.

title: T20: Design the target baseline schema
body:
**Not a translation.** Because the project deploys fresh, the schema can be restructured for free — bake in the media-type-generic core (§5), the P5 profile-provenance tables, and the P6 explainable-decision records now. Doing this later costs a migration chain and a backfill.

**Acceptance:** schema reviewed and agreed before T21 lands.

title: T21: Collapse 18 migrations to one baseline
body:
Fresh deploy, no upgrade path to preserve.

**Acceptance:** single `001_baseline.sql`; a fresh container reaches `/health` from an empty database.

title: T22: Swap sqlx driver and rename stackarr-postgres
body:
`sqlx` feature `postgres` -> `mysql` (MariaDB 11.4 LTS, per D2); 173 `PgPool`/`Postgres` refs -> `MySqlPool`. Much of this is concentrated in the dedicated `stackarr-postgres` crate (1,216 LOC), which becomes `stackarr-mariadb` — a real structural advantage.

**Acceptance:** workspace compiles against MariaDB.

title: T23: Convert 1,420 positional placeholders
body:
`$1..$n` -> `?`. **The trap:** `$1` may legally repeat or appear out of order within a query; `?` is positional-by-occurrence. A naive regex rewrite silently mis-binds.

**Acceptance:** conversion script **fails loudly** on repeated or non-monotonic placeholders rather than converting them; flagged queries hand-rewritten; all 1,060 tests green.

title: T24: Rewrite 78 RETURNING sites
body:
MySQL has no `RETURNING`. Each becomes `INSERT` + `SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID()` in a transaction, or an insert plus a re-select on a natural key.

D2 resolved: **MariaDB 11.4 LTS**, which supports `RETURNING` on `INSERT` — you may use it here to cut the rewrite. **New code must still be `RETURNING`-free** for portability.

**Acceptance:** every site hand-reviewed; no silent behaviour change under concurrency.

title: T25: Rewrite 77 ON CONFLICT clauses
body:
-> `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` / `INSERT IGNORE`. Semantics differ; upsert-with-condition needs care.

**Acceptance:** tests cover each upsert path.

title: T26: Convert JSON and identity column types
body:
56 `jsonb` refs -> `JSON`. Schema: `BIGSERIAL`/`SERIAL` -> `BIGINT`/`INT AUTO_INCREMENT`; `gen_random_uuid()` -> app-side UUID generation (portable).

**Acceptance:** schema and Rust types agree; JSON query paths tested.

title: T27: Apply GPL-3.0 headers
body:
D3 resolved: **GPL-3.0**.

**Acceptance:** headers applied consistently; CI check optional but preferred.

title: T28: Wire coverage-watchdog as a ratchet
body:
`coverage-watchdog` already exists in the workspace and is unused here.

**Acceptance:** per-crate coverage recorded; CI fails if the number drops.

title: T29: CI doc-drift check
body:
Assert `CLAUDE.md`'s crate list and workspace-member claims match `Cargo.toml`. Depends on T6 having corrected the file first.

**Acceptance:** check fails on a deliberately stale doc.

title: T30: Capturing proxy for live arr traffic
body:
Record real HTTP traffic from live Sonarr/Radarr/Prowlarr, including what Overseerr, Bazarr, Recyclarr, nzb360 and Homepage actually call.

**Acceptance:** a capture session produces replayable, redacted request/response pairs.

title: T31: Golden-file store at contracts/arr-v3/
body:
Adopt rdpapp's `contracts/` pattern — frozen, versioned, reviewed artefacts.

**Acceptance:** captures stored as golden files; a diff is a build failure, never silent drift.

title: T32: Replay and structural-diff harness
body:
Fire recorded requests at StackArr; diff JSON structurally (schema + shape), tolerant of ids and timestamps.

**Acceptance:** `just conformance` runs and reports a coverage percentage.

title: T33: Generate a failing test per OpenAPI path
body:
419 paths across Sonarr v3 (162), Radarr v3 (164) and Prowlarr v1 (93). All red initially — this is the red-first step of §6.2 at scale.

**Acceptance:** one test per path, all present, all failing for the right reason.

title: T34: Ranked backlog generator
body:
**The most valuable output of P2.** Intersect recorded real-client traffic with the §2.3 resource gap; emit one issue per unimplemented endpoint, ranked by actual usage.

This is why Appendix B is a placeholder — priority is measured, not guessed.

**Acceptance:** issues created and milestoned; Appendix B filled in.

title: T35: stackarr-compat-core skeleton
body:
Establish the façade rule: compat crates contain DTOs, route wiring and translation **only**. Any logic belongs in core.

**Acceptance:** crate exists; rule documented and enforceable at review.

title: T36: Arr authentication
body:
`X-Api-Key` header **and** `?apikey=` querystring, plus the forms-auth cookie for browser clients.

**Acceptance:** all three paths tested against golden captures.

title: T37: ProviderResource field reflection
body:
The arr UI and Prowlarr build settings forms from the `fields[]` array returned by provider endpoints — including `selectOptions`, `privacy`, `hidden` and **ordering**. Shape must match exactly.

**Acceptance:** golden-file match for indexer, download-client and notification providers.

title: T38: SignalR hub
body:
`/signalr/messages` — negotiate handshake plus JSON hub protocol over WebSocket. nzb360, LunaSea and the arr web UIs depend on it. Not optional.

**Acceptance:** nzb360 connects and receives live queue updates.

title: T39: Sonarr v3 façade — GET endpoints
body:
Priority order comes from T34. Expect `system/status`, `rootfolder`, `diskspace`, `health`, `series`, `episode`, `qualityprofile`, `tag`, `queue`, `history`, `calendar`, `parse`.

**Acceptance:** conformance green for the GET subset.

title: T40: Radarr v3 façade — GET endpoints
body:
Same shape as T39 over the film domain. Note `movie`, `collection`, `alttitle`, `credit` are Radarr-specific.

**Acceptance:** conformance green for the GET subset.

title: T41: Prowlarr v1 façade — GET endpoints
body:
**Deliberately omit `applications` and `appprofile`** — unification removes the sync problem they exist to solve. Document the omission in API-COMPATIBILITY.md.

**Acceptance:** conformance green for the GET subset; omissions documented, not silently missing.

title: T42: qualitydefinition resource
body:
`customformat` already exists (migration `014_custom_format_fields.sql`), which de-risks P5. `qualitydefinition` does not.

**Acceptance:** resource exposed on both Sonarr and Radarr façades; Recyclarr can read it.

title: T43: Write path across all three façades
body:
POST/PUT/DELETE.

**Acceptance:** Overseerr can add a series and a movie; Recyclarr can write.

title: T44: manualimport, rename, command, release
body:
`command` is the arr task-queue endpoint that many clients poll.

**Acceptance:** conformance green; nzb360 can trigger a search and see progress.

title: T45: Harden the migration importers
body:
`stackarr-migrate` (4,409 LOC) already has Sonarr/Radarr/Prowlarr importers. Add the SABnzbd importer available in `nzb-core::sabnzbd_import`.

**Acceptance:** a real Sonarr + Radarr + Prowlarr install migrates in one command and continues operating.

title: T46: Expose embedded engines over legacy download-client protocols
body:
SABnzbd-compatible and qBittorrent-WebUI-compatible APIs. Gives the façade's `downloadclient` resource something real to point at — **and** lets an existing Sonarr use StackArr as its download client with zero changes.

Cheapest possible on-ramp: adopt the download half before committing to the arr half.

**Acceptance:** a stock Sonarr successfully grabs and imports via StackArr.

title: T47: stackarr-profiles crate
body:
Subscribed profiles as first-class objects: upstream ref + local overrides.

**Acceptance:** a TRaSH profile can be subscribed to and applied.

title: T48: Three-way merge on upstream profile update
body:
**The headline feature.** Recyclarr and Configarr clobber local edits; we merge, with diff preview and changelog.

**Acceptance:** an upstream update that touches a locally-overridden score produces a reviewable diff, not a silent overwrite.

title: T49: Custom-format provenance
body:
Record source, version and override history: 'from TRaSH 2026-07-14, score overridden 500 -> 350'.

**Acceptance:** provenance visible per format via API and UI.

title: T50: Compiled custom-format scoring
body:
Replace N formats x M regexes per release per indexer per RSS cycle with a single-pass `RegexSet`/Aho-Corasick match. A genuine hot path that scales with how seriously a user takes TRaSH.

**Acceptance:** benchmark against the current implementation on a realistic TRaSH set.

title: T51: Profile-change simulation
body:
**Nobody else can build this.** 'Show me what would have been grabbed differently over the last 90 days if I applied this profile change.' Requires history and the release cache in one database — which we have.

**Acceptance:** a profile diff produces a historical impact report before it is applied.

title: T52: Port ProfSync wizard logic
body:
`myotherrepos/ArrProfileGenerator` (ProfSync) already solves TRaSH profile generation in Python — 12 questions to a complete config. Translate, do not redesign.

**Acceptance:** equivalent guided setup available natively.

title: T53: Port the Sonarr parser test corpus first
body:
4,644 LOC of parser tests are the richest spec asset in the reference repos. `stackarr-parser` is 1,838 LOC with 175 tests against Sonarr's 4,519 LOC.

**Port the tests first, then grow the parser to pass them.** Expect this to be the single largest body of work in the plan.

**Acceptance:** ported corpus passes.

title: T54: Port the 30 DecisionEngine specifications
body:
Order-sensitive, twelve years of accreted edge cases.

**Acceptance:** each specification has ported tests that pass; ordering verified.

title: T55: Explainable decisions
body:
Emit a structured, replayable object with the full per-specification score breakdown, exposed as an API resource. Sonarr's rejection reasons are strings in a log; 'why didn't it grab this?' is the most common complaint in the arr community.

A headline feature disguised as a refactor.

**Acceptance:** every grab/reject decision is queryable with its full reasoning.

title: T56: Metadata: TVDB/TMDB direct, scene numbering, XEM
body:
Skyhook is Sonarr-operated infrastructure we cannot use. Going direct means API keys, differing data shapes, and — critically — scene numbering and XEM mapping, **where naive rewrites break and never recover.**

Budget as a project in itself.

**Acceptance:** scene-numbered series resolve correctly against a known-hard fixture set.

title: T57: Unified indexer query planner
body:
One cache, one rate limiter, one query plan across all media types. Today Sonarr and Radarr independently hammer the same tracker with separate limiters — fewer requests here means materially lower ban risk.

**Acceptance:** measured reduction in duplicate indexer requests.

title: T58: Declarative notification and import-list providers
body:
~100 unique providers across the three apps is the majority of the boring work and it never stops. Most notifications are an HTTP POST with a body template; most import lists are a fetch-and-parse.

Making these **data rather than code** collapses roughly 60% of the tail (§7.5).

**Acceptance:** at least 10 notification providers defined purely as templates.

title: T59: Unified download queue and resource budgets
body:
One queue, one disk budget, one bandwidth budget. Today the arrs fight each other for client slots and free space.

**Acceptance:** a global priority ordering across TV and film; disk reservations honoured across media types.
